clue.text: Dark colour around the motorway is rock

indicators.note: around says the colour word wraps itself about the road's abbreviation

blocks.note: puce is a dark purplish-brown colour
the M1, Britain's first motorway, written as MI

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured stone lies beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; crosswords write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light porous volcanic stone, so it is a kind of rock.

clue.text: Following father, Linda turns out a champion

indicators.note: the name turns out differently, so its letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
the name supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Linda follows in her father's footsteps and becomes a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following father' places the rearranged name after PA.
explanation.definitionFit: A paladin was one of Charlemagne's knights, hence a heroic defender of a cause.

clue.text: Lady doctor's rowdy celebration

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a rag is a boisterous student celebration or prank

explanation.surface: A woman doctor holds a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a student rag is a week of noisy charity stunts.
explanation.definitionFit: Morag is a Scottish woman's first name, so it stands for a lady.

clue.text: Hats (not soft) and footwear worn in ministry

definitions.note: describes the garment rather than naming it

indicators.note: not tells you to remove the musical abbreviation for soft from the headgear

blocks.note: caps are hats
p is piano, the musical marking for soft
a sock is worn on the foot

explanation.surface: Hats and shoes as items of clerical dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock is the long robe clergy wear when serving in church.

clue.text: Note, for example, increase and work out takings

blocks.note: a banknote is an example of cash
to up is to increase

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper notes rising sales and totals the day's money.
explanation.walkthrough: To cash up is the British phrase for counting the till at closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashing up means counting the money a shop has taken at the end of trading.

clue.text: Flourish with a bounce

blocks.note: taken as written
a bound is a leap or bounce

explanation.surface: Something thrives with a spring in its step.
explanation.definitionFit: To abound is to exist in large numbers, to thrive in plenty.

clue.text: Where one lives only on water?

definitions.text: Where one lives only on water?

blocks.clueFragment: Where one lives only on water?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone surviving on a diet of nothing but water

blocks.clueFragment: Where one lives only on water?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a home that floats, sitting on a river or canal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives only on water' suggests a starvation diet; read 'on' literally and it is a dwelling afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseboat is a vessel fitted out as a home, moored on a river or canal.

clue.text: Man, say, enters into wage pattern

indicators.note: enters into places one word inside the other

blocks.note: pay is a wage
the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man takes up a wage agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley is the swirling teardrop design used on fabrics, a recognised pattern.

clue.text: Up-to-the-minute condition of gallery's work

blocks.note: first meaning: the most modern, using the latest technology
second meaning, read literally: the state a gallery's art is in

explanation.surface: A report on the current condition of a gallery's paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for the most advanced stage of development, and literally the condition of artwork.

clue.text: Slight stain

blocks.note: first meaning: an insult or disparaging remark
second meaning: a blot on someone's reputation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as an adjective modifying stain, but it is a noun meaning an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insulting remark, and also a mark of disgrace on a person's character.

clue.text: Having drunk tots, miscue and produce strain

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and staggering, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drinker downs tots, fluffs a snooker shot and strains with effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Tots are small drinks of spirits; a miscue is a bad snooker or billiards shot. 'Strain' is a tune here.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose music for words is to produce a strain, an old word for a melody.

clue.text: Girl taking turn round island in slow movement

indicators.note: round says the word for a turn goes about the island letter

blocks.note: Ada is a girl's name
a go is a turn in a game
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A girl turns around an island at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a piece or section of music played slowly, a slow movement of a work.

clue.text: Still, yen in exchange is superficially attractive

indicators.note: an exchange swaps things around, so the letters change places

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A currency dealer notes that the yen, still traded, looks attractive on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' suggests currency trading alongside yen, but it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel glitters but is cheap, so tinselly describes something showy yet of little worth.

clue.text: Being initiated, somehow we think on

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be put together differently

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Newcomers being inducted keep pondering somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone initiated has been let into a secret, so they possess inside information.

clue.text: Hearty dances?

blocks.note: surface reading: lively, vigorous dancing
setter's reading: dances of hearties, an old word for sailors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' looks like an adjective, but 'my hearties' is how sailors are addressed, so these are sailors' dances.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is the lively solo dance traditionally performed by sailors aboard ship.

clue.text: Bring back tackle with young fish

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: a fishing rod is part of an angler's tackle
Y is the abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: An angler brings home their tackle and a small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The dory, or John Dory, is an edible sea fish with a flat body.

clue.text: Fairy in super "Iolanthe" production

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the opera's name
surface padding: it completes the picture of a staged show

explanation.surface: A fairy appears in a superb staging of Gilbert and Sullivan's Iolanthe.
explanation.walkthrough: Iolanthe is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta whose heroine is a fairy, and its subtitle is 'The Peer and the Peri'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a peri is a beautiful supernatural being, so the word means a fairy.

clue.text: Precise, if shapeless, formula produces something flowery

indicators.note: shapeless means without form, so that word is taken out of the next one

blocks.note: prim means stiffly precise and proper
taken as written before the removal

explanation.surface: A rigid formula without structure somehow yields floral prose.
explanation.walkthrough: Shapeless is read as minus FORM, which leaves ULA from formula.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula is a plant genus that includes primroses and cowslips, so it is a flower.

clue.text: Criticism follows when I replace you, they say, in the organisation

indicators.note: replace tells you one letter swaps into the place of another
they say means as spoken, so a word stands for the letter it sounds like

blocks.note: structure is the way something is organised
taken as written
the letter U sounds like the word you

explanation.surface: Someone is criticised for taking over another person's job in a company.
explanation.walkthrough: In the word for organisation the letter U is swapped out for I.
explanation.definitionFit: A stricture is a critical remark or censure, so it means criticism.

clue.text: Makes up in passages

blocks.note: taken as written
vents are passages for air or smoke

explanation.surface: Someone fabricates stories while lurking in corridors.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up something is to create or fabricate it, the sense of invents.

clue.text: Bird, not dead, to take on new life

indicators.note: not means leave out the letter for dead from the bird's name

blocks.note: the redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A bird thought dead comes back to life.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to begin again, which is taking on a fresh lease of life.

clue.text: Pet to lick tail?

blocks.note: to lap is to lick up liquid
to dog or tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A pet dog licking its own tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pampered dog kept as a companion animal at home.

clue.text: Sack man, reversing position

indicators.note: reversing turns the man's name back to front

blocks.note: Sid is a man's name
a place is a position

explanation.surface: A boss fires a worker, swapping someone else into the role.
explanation.definitionFit: To displace someone is to remove them from their job or post, as sacking does.

clue.text: Travelling case for one taking part in dance

indicators.note: taking part in puts the numeral inside the dance word

blocks.note: valse is the French word for waltz, used in English
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A case packed for a dancer on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small suitcase or travelling bag.

clue.text: Ridge was in front, for example, when climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means read upwards, so the abbreviation runs backwards

blocks.note: to have led is to have been in front
e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: A climber who was leading reaches a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow shelf of rock, which a ridge also describes as a raised edge.

clue.text: Worked on tyres even - and exercised with weights

blocks.note: tyres are pumped up with air
to iron is to make even or smooth

explanation.surface: Someone inflated their tyres evenly, then went to the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumping iron is the slang idiom for lifting weights in training.

clue.text: Drop a small weight

blocks.note: first meaning: a small measure of spirits
second meaning: a unit of weight, one-sixteenth of an ounce

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to let go of a weight; 'Drop' is a noun for a nip of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dram is a small drink of whisky and also an old apothecaries' unit of weight.

clue.text: Distribute gin, perhaps, by a ship

indicators.note: perhaps marks the drink's letters as one possible arrangement among others

blocks.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Gin is handed round beside a moored ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin, perhaps' looks like 'a spirit, for example', but here perhaps marks the letters of gin to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign is to allot or allocate, handing out shares or tasks.

clue.text: Air point of view

blocks.note: first meaning: appearance or manner
second meaning: a particular way of considering a matter

explanation.surface: Someone voices their opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect means a look or bearing, like an air, and also a facet or viewpoint on an issue.
